https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/18.text: Listen (3 mins) Save Share Russia seizes assets of French firms, summons UK envoy over Ukraine support on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham, right, and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [Simon Jones/Pool Photo via AP] By AFP and Reuters Published On 18 Sep 2026 18 Sep 2026 Russia has stepped up pressure on Ukraine’s allies, summoning Britain’s top diplomat in Moscow over arms shipments to Kyiv and seizing Russian assets of several Western firms. The Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Britain’s charge d’affairs, Danae Dholakia, on Friday, issuing a formal protest over the UK’s “further increase” in weapons to Ukraine. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Russia ‘sabotaging’ power supply lines at Zaporizhzhia plant: Greenpeace list 2 of 3 India warns new US tariffs over Russian oil could impact ties list 3 of 3 Russia’s plans may include strikes against Ukraine’s allies, Poland says end of list “London is placing itself in the position of an accomplice to the bloody atrocities committed by the Kyiv regime, which can only be characterised as terrorism and war crimes,” the ministry said in a statement. Britain has maintained its support for Ukraine and says it will stand “shoulder to shoulder” with Kyiv and will provide whatever military equipment it needs, saying just last month that it will share classified weapons information. Moscow’s move comes the day after Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Russia might be preparing to launch hybrid drone and missile strikes against countries that support Ukraine, including Poland. He said that such attacks would be framed as accidental, with the intention of weakening NATO states’ resolve to invoke collective defence provisions in the event of an attack on one of its countries. French President Emmanuel Macron said on Friday that the threat posed by Russia’s shadow operations was growing across Europe and that Moscow had targeted ⁠⁠France with hybrid attacks in the past few ⁠⁠weeks. “The Russian hybrid threat against Europeans and against France has intensified,” he said after a meeting with French political leaders. Advertisement France’s interior minister had met regional prefects to step up “vigilance in response to the Russian hybrid attacks”, Macron said, adding that he had ordered “the government to prepare a plan to protect our critical infrastructure” and the “most sensitive” defence industry and technology sites against drone and cyber-attacks. Moscow seizes French, Swiss firms As Russia steps up pressure on Ukraine’s political allies, it is also targeting Western companies. Moscow has ordered the seizure of Russian businesses and assets of Swiss food giant Nestle and three French firms: retailer Auchan, DIY chain Lemana Pro (formerly Leroy Merlin) and logistics firm FM Logistics. President Vladimir Putin signed a decree late on Thursday that changed the firms’ Russian operations to a new entity, LEV Management, which is managed by a Russian Ministry of Interior general, according to Novaya Gazeta Europe. Nestle said it was still “assessing” the situation and its options but it remains “committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights”. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Friday that one of the reasons behind the decision was because Nestle and Auchan are companies from “unfriendly” countries. Their assets are only under “temporary administration” and that no decisions have been taken as of yet, Peskov added. Overnight Russian strikes hit multiple regions in Ukraine, sparking several fires across the country, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is to host the inaugural Carpathian Eight summit of several European countries. They include Romania, Poland, Slovakia, Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary and Serbia, with the European Union also set to discuss regional cooperation. Hungary and Slovakia have refused to send Kyiv direct military assistance in the past, though Poland and Romania remain staunch allies.

https://bnn-news.com/money/while-the-us-.text: Photo: Kaspars Nordens/LETA Advertisements Opinion article While the United States is looking for opportunities to buy cheaper fertilisers from Belarus and protect the interests of its farmers, economically complex issues in Latvia are still too often addressed with loud political slogans. US President Donald Trump has announced that Washington is working on a broader deal with Belarus, including on fertilisers. The US president may also be taking into account the fact that the 12 million tonnes of fertilisers Belarus is currently forced to export through Russian railways and ports generate around 576 million US dollars a year for Russia, much of which ultimately feeds the aggressor state’s war machine. This is in the interests of neither global security nor the economies of the Baltic states. Latvia therefore needs to start seriously discussing what the decisions we make ourselves are costing the Latvian economy. Cargo is not just about trains and ships. It also means business for ports, railways, terminals, freight operators and hundreds of companies connected to the sector. It means jobs, wages and tax revenue. Advertisements The Latvian Stevedoring Companies Association warns of a simple reality: if Latvia unilaterally turns away cargo, that does not mean the cargo disappears. It can find other routes and other ports. According to the Association, the result could be a situation in which Russian exports continue while Latvia loses cargo, revenue and jobs. Moreover, once a country loses its place on the international logistics map, winning it back is not easy. When cargo owners establish new routes, find new partners and sign new contracts, there is no reason to assume they will automatically return to Latvia a few years later. Latvia therefore needs to stop addressing these issues through slogans alone. Every new restriction should come with clear answers to two simple questions: what will it actually change, and who will pay the price? Advertisements If international policy is changing and even the United States is looking for new avenues of economic cooperation with Belarus, Latvia must assess not only the political message sent by its decisions but also their economic consequences. Otherwise, others may redraw the map of cooperation while we reduce our own place on it. Cargo can leave quickly. Jobs can leave with it. But regaining Latvia’s place in international transit could take years. Ukraine: Russian strike kills two teenage girls in Chernihiv Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 30 October 2026 - 0:15 GMT+1 A Russian strike on Chernihiv killed two 15-year-old girls and injured 25 people, local officials say. Meanwhile, a US-brokered ceasefire in southern Ukraine is allowing demining work aimed at opening humanitarian routes. … More Firefighters rushed to extinguish burning cars and tackle flames and smoke pouring from damaged buildings, while emergency crews attended to victims amid scattered debris. Footage shows rescuers carrying a person into an ambulance and a body lying under a blanket near the scene. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The local military administration said the attack involved a Banderol cruise missile , a relatively inexpensive jet-powered weapon capable of loitering before striking its target. Businesses, homes and vehicles were damaged in the attack. The strike came as a separate, US-brokered ceasefire in southern Ukraine was reported to be holding around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky , in the Kherson region . Ukrainian and Russian human rights ombudsmen said on Wednesday that the local truce had passed 30 hours without an incident . Images released by Russia's Defence Ministry purportedly show military engineers clearing mines near Oleshky , although the filming date was not provided. The operation is intended to open routes for humanitarian aid and allow residents who wish to leave to do so. Around 2,000 people are believed to remain in the city, where food, water and medicine have been scarce for months. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed the respite but said the evacuation of civilians would be crucial to the truce's success . https://dupagepolicyjournal.com/roselle-.text: ← Back to the wire Roselle announces community events, contests, and programs for late October and November Roselle is hosting a variety of fall events, including a scarecrow contest, community fundraisers, and the annual Turkey Trot 5K. The Village also highlights public works initiatives and safety reminders for Halloween. Residents are encouraged to participate in local programs and meetings. 12:39 p.m. Friday, Oct 16 By DuPage Policy Journal David Pileski, Mayor at Village of Roselle | Official Website Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email The Village of Roselle has announced a series of community events and programs taking place throughout late October and November. Residents are invited to participate in the Great Roselle Scarecrow Contest, with entries due by October 18 and displays ready by October 24. The Roselle Arts and Culture Foundation is organizing the event at Petal Plaza, welcoming families, businesses, and local groups to join at no cost. The next Village Board meeting is scheduled for October 26 at Village Hall, beginning at 7:00 p.m. Attendees can provide live comments during the meeting. The Village also continues its Shared Cost Parkway Tree Program, allowing residents to request additional trees for their parkways. Interested participants must complete the program’s interest form by November 15 to be considered for the 2027 planting season. Public Works will contact those who express interest when planning begins. October 15 marks "Imagine a Day without Water," highlighting the importance of reliable water service. Public Works maintains Roselle’s water system, which includes four pump stations, three storage tanks, two emergency interconnections with neighboring communities, over 101 miles of water main, more than 1,400 water main valves, and over 1,300 fire hydrants. "No water = No clean hands, no washed produce, no coffee... Clean water is more than a convenience; it's something we rely on every day!" according to the Village of Roselle. Halloween trick-or-treat hours are set for October 31 from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. The Village encourages adults to help children remain visible to vehicles, especially after sunset, and recommends using reflective tape or glow sticks. Drivers are urged to exercise caution and watch for children crossing streets. Additional community events include the Roselle Sister Cities Italian Committee’s Dine to Donate fundraiser at Rosario’s Pizzeria & Catering on October 19, the Bloomingdale/Roselle Rotary Club’s Trunk or Treat on October 24, and the Enchanted Masquerade Gala hosted by the RSCA Polish Committee on the same evening. The American Legion Auxiliary Unit 1084 will run its Giving Tree program from November 13 through December 4, collecting gifts for local veterans, children, and families. Registration is also open for the 12th Annual Roselle Turkey Trot 5K, taking place on Thanksgiving Day, November 26, with proceeds supporting scholarships for attendees.
